Harry Bush (born Henry Bush) was an English first-class cricketer who played during the late 19th century. Here is what is known about his life and career:

### Biographical Details
*   **Full Name:** Henry Bush
*   **Born:** August 8, 1850, in Clifton, Bristol, England
*   **Died:** December 16, 1934, in Clifton, Bristol, England

### Cricket Career
Harry Bush was a right-handed batsman and a wicket-keeper whose first-class career was relatively brief but notable for the era. His activities primarily centered around the **Gloucestershire County Cricket Club**.

*   **First-Class Career:** He played first-class cricket between 1874 and 1880.
*   **Role:** He was primarily a wicket-keeper.
*   **Teams:** He played exclusively for Gloucestershire.

**Statistical Summary (First-Class):**
*   **Matches:** He played in 17 first-class matches.
*   **Batting:** He scored 161 runs at an average of 6.44. His highest score was 24.
*   **Wicket-keeping:** As a wicket-keeper, he claimed 19 catches and made 11 stumpings—a solid record for that period in the game.

### Historical Context & Note on Confusion
It is important to note that information on Victorian-era cricketers like Harry Bush can sometimes be sparse. Because he was a contemporary of the legendary W.G. Grace and the Grace family, who dominated Gloucestershire cricket during that time, records from that era focus heavily on the famous players of the time, often relegating consistent, professional domestic players like Bush to the background.

**Important Distinction:**
There is sometimes confusion between different cricketers of the same era with similar names. It is vital to ensure you are looking at the Henry "Harry" Bush who played for Gloucestershire (1850–1934) and not other minor players or amateurs who may have shared the name in local leagues. His records are officially maintained by organizations like *ESPNcricinfo* and *CricketArchive*, which confirm his identity as a Gloucestershire stalwart of the mid-1870s.

### Summary
Harry Bush was a solid, if not spectacular, county cricketer who served Gloucestershire during their formative years as a first-class club. After his playing days concluded in 1880, he maintained a lower profile, spending the remainder of his life in Clifton, Bristol, where he eventually passed away in 1934 at the age of 84.
